I would keep to the cropping pattern I know best in Quzhou: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That is the safest way for me to use my fields, labor, and water. I would not spread myself across many crops, because I am older and I would rather manage two familiar crops well than take risks on something more complicated. For wheat, I would rely on improved seed, put most of my fertilizer before sowing and at jointing, irrigate at the key stages if water is available, and keep weeds, aphids, and rust under control with a small number of pesticide sprays. After wheat harvest, I would move quickly into summer maize, use hybrid seed for stable yield, keep fertilizer simple, irrigate when the crop is establishing and around the big demand period, and watch closely for armyworm, corn borer, and leaf disease. I would use ploughing before wheat if the soil is hard, and then rotary tillage or quick seedbed preparation between wheat and maize so I do not lose time.
